what_it_says: A model with no memory token cannot use memory it is handed: arm A, which never saw a memory conversation, shows memory_shown_when_installed 0.0 at both seeds -- engine.py's span.session_start_ids has nothing to force in without the token, exactly as DAWNR-MEMORY.md section 8 and memory_eval.py's own docstring predict; this is the baseline the with/without comparison needs, not a result about arm B.

Recall transferred, at a seed-dependent rate: with the span installed, arm B answers 'what do you remember about me?' from the span 68% of the time at seed 1337 and 25% at seed 1338 (mean 0.46 of 28 held-out items per seed); with no span installed it answers 'nothing yet' 100% of the time at both seeds, and never invents a preference with nothing in the store to have grounded it (recall_invented_without_span 0.0 both seeds). Both halves of the recall family (say what is remembered, and say nothing when there is nothing) moved from arm A's 0.0 baseline.

The rename families (use what is remembered, the person's current words beat memory) did not transfer at 197 rows over 400 steps: preference_following_with_span and message_over_memory are 0.0 for both arms at both seeds -- the model is not renaming the sequence parameter at all yet, span or no span, message or no message (followed_name also requires the program to still pass the task's own examples, so a rename that broke the program would not be credited either; the rows are too few relative to the 1,007 tool conversations already in the same 400 steps to move a rewrite this specific).

unapplied_unchanged (a style preference over a task it does not touch, program should be unchanged) went the wrong way at seed 1337 (0.0, worse than arm A's 0.21) and stayed below arm A at seed 1338 too (0.14 vs 0.14 at scale, mean 0.07 vs 0.18): arm B changes the program more often when nothing in memory should touch it, the opposite of what this family is meant to teach; not enough data yet to tell this apart from noise at two seeds, but it is not a win and is reported as one.

The t-task guard holds at both seeds (pass_all_133 13/13 then 14/15, both within -2 of arm A; dev_well_formed 34/27 and 22/38, both within -5): adding the 197 memory conversations to the tool track's own mix did not cost the guard the tool conversations already passed. That is a necessary condition for keeping this data, not a claim that the memory behaviours themselves are learned: recall moved, the two rename families did not, and unapplied moved against.
recommendation: Memory conversations stay opt-in for now (dawnr_pipeline.py --extra-conversations), same as the tool conversations: the guard holds, so training on them costs nothing measured on the 133 prompts, but only one of the four families (recall) shows a clear with/without gap at this size (197 rows, 400 steps, two seeds); more rows targeted at the rename families is the next thing to try before claiming 'use what is remembered' or 'the person's current words beat memory' are learned.
